loci.rationale: preference() records the insights on/off choice and, on withdrawal, cancels queued 'report' jobs scoped to the withdrawing owner's cases; enabled() reads the latest choice row, making withdrawal the effective state.

drain() re-checks enabled(owner,'insights') at execution time before generating a report, so a withdrawn owner's queued or re-queued report is not produced, while the unaffected borrower's report still runs; restricted cases are skipped.
The 'report' action requires insights enabled before queueing, so opt-in is the precondition for queuing a report job.
NOTICE informs the user beforehand that insights and promotions each require separate optional consent, can be switched off as easily as on, and that withdrawal applies to future processing.
Renders the privacy-choices section with the notice and a single symmetric 'Switch off'/'Switch on' form per purpose via the same /preference route, satisfying equal-ease withdrawal.
Owner-facing queue controls: 'Queue repayment report' and 'Process pending tasks' (drain), showing the entrypoint that triggers report generation and the drain that must respect withdrawal.
Routes /preference to store.preference and case actions (including drain) to store.action, connecting the UI toggles and drain to the assessed logic.

output.path_summary: Opt-in is recorded via /preference -> store.preference (choices row) and a report job is queued via the case 'report' action (store.action, gated on enabled insights). Withdrawal uses the same /preference route with value 'off', which inserts a new choice row and cancels queued 'report' jobs for that owner's cases only. On each drain, store.drain re-checks enabled(owner,'insights') before generating a report, so the withdrawing borrower's queued/re-queued report is not produced, while the other borrower's consent remains on and their report is generated. Prior information is supplied by NOTICE rendered in the privacy-choices section.
missing_boundaries: No explicit retry mechanism is modeled; only queued-state cancellation plus the execution-time consent re-check cover re-drains. Retry semantics beyond re-draining queued jobs are unavailable.
No runtime execution was performed; conclusions are static readings of the supplied source.
Restriction (restricted flag) is a separate control and not the withdrawal mechanism assessed here.
